answer: A general payment suspension lasts for a 180 calendar day period, and if more time is needed CPI may approve up to an additional 180 calendar days, but general suspensions shall not continue beyond 360 calendar days. It can last longer only if CPI approves changing it from a general suspension to a fraud suspension.

citations.quote: If CPI approves a general suspension, it will be for a 180 calendar day period.
Only CPI may approve the request to extend the period of the payment suspension for up to an additional 180 calendar days upon the written request of the UPIC.
General suspensions shall not continue beyond 360 calendar days.
Only with CPI approval may the category of the type of payment suspension be transitioned from a general payment suspension to a fraud suspension.

gold_answer: An approved general suspension lasts 180 calendar days. CPI can extend it once by up to another 180 days, and a general suspension cannot run past 360 calendar days in total.
gold_quote: If CPI approves a general suspension, it will be for a 180 calendar day period. The UPIC shall complete its medical review and any subsequent activities (i.e., statistical sampling extrapolation, draft overpayment determination notice, etc.) during the initial 180 days of a general suspension. CMS expects the medical reviews to be completed and the calculation of any potential overpayments to be determined before the end of the initial suspension period. Only in rare instances will an extension be granted.

judge.rationale: The answer matches the gold on the 180-day initial period, the single CPI-approved extension of up to 180 more days, and the 360-day cap, and it adds the general-to-fraud transition point, all of which appear in the cited passage P2.
